text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VIETNAM NEWS
-- Vietnam and Bangladesh have signed a trade agreement for 1996-1999, the two countries' first such accord since they established diplomatic relations in 1973.
-- At least 10 people died on Monday and Tuesday after Typhoon Willie hit Vietnam's central provinces of Ha Tinh and Nghe An on Sunday.
-- Ministers from Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand and Burma began a two-day forestry meeting in Hanoi on Tuesday.
-- An agreement between Vietnam and Bulgaria aimed at fostering and providing legal protection for investment has been signed in Sofia.
-- Nissan Motors Corp and Marubeni Trading Corp expect to receive a license this week to begin work on what will be the 14th automobile assembly plant in Vietnam.

-- The Ministry of Planning and Investment has granted licenses to 192 joint venture and wholly foreign-owned projects since the start of the year. Companies from Taiwan, South Korea and Singapore invested $669.1 million in 27 projects compared $531.4 million in 17 projects in 1995. - - - -
NHAN DAN
-- GATT's former director general, Arthur Dunkel, on Tuesday told Deputy Prime Minister Phan Van Khai that he supported Vietnam's bid to join the World Trade Organisation.
-- Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam arrived in New York to attend the 51st U.N General Assembly.

-- Typhoon Willie's torrential rains caused serious flooding in the central coastal province of Thanh Hoa. Some 2,800 ha of paddy field were submerged and roads, dykes and dams were seriously damaged.
-- Construction of the Yaly hydropower station in the central highland was seriously damaged by flash flooding. One worker was killed.
-- The Vietnam-Uzbekistan friendship assocation was established in Hanoi. - - - -
QUAN DOI NHAN DAN

-- Vietnam's Chief of Staff, Pham Van Tra, on Tuesday began a five-day offical friendship visit to Laos. A Laotian military delegation led by General Political Commissar Khanphuong Chanthaphoma on Tuesday began an official friendship visit to Vietnam.
-- One hundred and sixty-three press articles about traffic safety were granted awards by the Directing Board for Transport Safety and the Vietnam Journalists' Association. - - - -
HA NOI MOI
-- The South Korean government donated equipment worth $226,314 to Hanoi's Technical industry school.
-- The United Nations Development Programme and the Vietnamese government are holding a three-day colloquium on public administration reform in Hanoi.
